why: Removing the first occurrence of a value from a list is O(n) each time, too slow for 2 * 10^5 queries. Instead keep, per value, a queue of the positions where it lives (a hash map of deques) and mark removed slots as dead; the final cart is the live slots in order.
hints: list.remove(x) scans from the front every time. With 2 * 10^5 operations, what does that cost in the worst case?

Never delete physically. Append every item to one growing array; for each value keep a deque of its positions in increasing order. Removing the first occurrence of v is popleft on v's deque plus marking that slot dead.
Hash map value -> deque of indices, a parallel alive array, O(1) per query, then one pass to output the live items. O(n + q) total.
pitfalls: Positions must stay in order: newly appended items go to the back of their value's deque, which keeps it sorted.
A removal for a value not in the cart should be ignored safely (empty or missing deque).
The query is negative; remove the item whose id is -query, not query.
